<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
 <modelVersion>
  4.0.0
 </modelVersion>
 <parent>
  <groupId>
   org.sonatype.oss
  </groupId>
  <artifactId>
   oss-parent
  </artifactId>
  <version>
   7
  </version>
 </parent>
 <groupId>
  com.google.auto
 </groupId>
 <artifactId>
  auto-parent
 </artifactId>
 <packaging>
  pom
 </packaging>
 <version>
  4-SNAPSHOT
 </version>
 <name>
  Auto (Parent)
 </name>
 <description>
  A collection of code generators for Java.
 </description>
 <url>
  https://github.com/google/auto
 </url>
 <properties>
  <project.build.sourceEncoding>
   UTF-8
  </project.build.sourceEncoding>
  <java.version>
   1.6
  </java.version>
 </properties>
 <scm>
  <url>
   http://github.com/google/auto
  </url>
  <connection>
   scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git
  </connection>
  <developerConnection>
   scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git
  </developerConnection>
  <tag>
   HEAD
  </tag>
 </scm>
 <issueManagement>
  <system>
   GitHub Issues
  </system>
  <url>
   http://github.com/google/auto/issues
  </url>
 </issueManagement>
 <licenses>
  <license>
   <name>
    Apache 2.0
   </name>
   <url>
    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt
   </url>
  </license>
 </licenses>
 <organization>
  <name>
   Google, Inc.
  </name>
  <url>
   http://www.google.com
  </url>
 </organization>
 <build>
  <plugins>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-compiler-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     3.1
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <source>
      ${java.version}
     </source>
     <target>
      ${java.version}
     </target>
     <compilerArgument>
      -Xlint:all
     </compilerArgument>
     <showWarnings>
      true
     </showWarnings>
     <showDeprecation>
      true
     </showDeprecation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-checkstyle-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     2.11
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <consoleOutput>
      true
     </consoleOutput>
     <configLocation>
      checkstyle.xml
     </configLocation>
     <failOnViolation>
      false
     </failOnViolation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
  </plugins>
  <pluginManagement>
   <plugins>
    <plugin>
     <artifactId>
      maven-invoker-plugin
     </artifactId>
     <version>
      1.8
     </version>
    </plugin>
   </plugins>
  </pluginManagement>
 </build>
 <profiles>
  <profile>
   <id>
    default-profile
   </id>
   <activation>
    <activeByDefault>
     true
    </activeByDefault>
    <file>
     <exists>
      ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
     </exists>
    </file>
   </activation>
   <properties>
    <toolsjar>
     ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
    </toolsjar>
   </properties>
  </profile>
  <profile>
   <id>
    mac-profile
   </id>
   <activation>
    <activeByDefault>
     false
    </activeByDefault>
    <file>
     <exists>
      ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar
     </exists>
    </file>
   </activation>
   <properties>
    <toolsjar>
     ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar
    </toolsjar>
   </properties>
  </profile>
 </profiles>
</project>

# Maven Dependency Resolution

## Overview
Maven is a build automation and dependency management tool for Java projects. It uses a Project Object Model (POM) file to manage dependencies, build configurations, and project metadata.

## Common Dependency Resolution Issues

### 1. Missing tools.jar in JDK 9+
**Problem**: Projects that depend on `com.sun:tools:jar` fail in JDK 9+ because tools.jar was removed.

**Background**:
- In JDK 8 and earlier, compiler tools were in `lib/tools.jar`
- In JDK 9+, these tools were modularized into `java.compiler` and `jdk.compiler` modules
- The file `tools.jar` no longer exists

**Solution Options**:

#### Option 1: Remove the dependency entirely (if not needed)
```xml
<!-- Remove this dependency if annotation processing tools aren't used -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

#### Option 2: Make it optional or use a profile
```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
  <optional>true</optional>
</dependency>
```

#### Option 3: Use profiles to conditionally include (best for cross-version compatibility)
```xml
<profiles>
  <profile>
    <id>jdk8</id>
    <activation>
      <jdk>1.8</jdk>
    </activation>
    <dependencies>
      <dependency>
        <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
        <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
        <scope>system</scope>
        <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
      </dependency>
    </dependencies>
  </profile>
</profiles>
```

#### Option 4: Provide a default property that won't fail
```xml
<properties>
  <toolsjar>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</toolsjar>
</properties>

<!-- Change to: -->
<properties>
  <toolsjar>${java.home}</toolsjar> <!-- Safe default that exists -->
</properties>
```

### 2. Version Conflicts
**Problem**: Multiple versions of the same artifact in the dependency tree

**Solution**: Use `<dependencyManagement>` section
```xml
<dependencyManagement>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>18.0</version>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>
```

### 3. Repository Accessibility
**Problem**: Artifacts not found in Maven Central

**Solution**: Add custom repositories
```xml
<repositories>
  <repository>
    <id>central</id>
    <url>https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2</url>
  </repository>
</repositories>
```

## Useful Maven Commands

```bash
# Clean and compile
mvn clean compile

# Skip tests
mvn clean install -DskipTests

# Show dependency tree
mvn dependency:tree

# Show effective POM (with all inherited settings)
mvn help:effective-pom

# Debug dependency resolution
mvn dependency:resolve -X

# Update snapshots
mvn clean install -U
```

## System Scope Dependencies

System scope dependencies require an absolute path to a JAR file:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>1.8</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

**Warning**: System scope is deprecated and should be avoided when possible. It's not portable across different systems.

# Java Version Compatibility

## Java Version History and Breaking Changes

### JDK 8 (LTS)
- Last version with `tools.jar` in `lib/` directory
- Included annotation processing tools bundled
- System property: `java.version` = 1.8.x

### JDK 9
- Introduced Java Platform Module System (JPMS)
- **Breaking**: Removed `tools.jar` - tools moved to modules
- Tools moved to `jdk.compiler` and `java.compiler` modules
- System property: `java.version` = 9.x

### JDK 11 (LTS)
- No `tools.jar` file
- Removed Java EE and CORBA modules
- System property: `java.version` = 11.x

### JDK 17 (LTS)
- Current recommended LTS version
- Sealed classes, pattern matching enhancements
- System property: `java.version` = 17.x

## Migrating from JDK 8 to JDK 9+

### 1. Tools.jar Migration

**Old code (JDK 8):**
```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

# Git Diff Format

## Overview
The unified diff format is used by Git, GNU diff, and patch utilities. It shows changes between files in a standardized, machine-readable format.

## Basic Structure

```diff
diff --git a/path/to/file.txt b/path/to/file.txt
index abc123..def456 100644
--- a/path/to/file.txt
+++ b/path/to/file.txt
@@ -line_start,num_lines +line_start,num_lines @@
 context line
-removed line
+added line
 context line
```

## Header Components

### 1. Git Diff Header
```diff
diff --git a/oldfile b/newfile
```
- Shows the comparison between two file versions
- Paths are relative to repository root

### 2. Index Line (optional for Git)
```diff
index abc123..def456 100644
```
- Shows Git object hashes and file mode
- Can be omitted in simple patches

### 3. File Markers
```diff
--- a/path/to/file.txt
+++ b/path/to/file.txt
```
- `---` indicates the original file (before changes)
- `+++` indicates the modified file (after changes)
- `a/` and `b/` are conventional prefixes (can vary)

### 4. Hunk Header
```diff
@@ -10,7 +10,8 @@
```
- Format: `@@ -start,count +start,count @@`
- `-start,count`: Starting line and number of lines in original file
- `+start,count`: Starting line and number of lines in modified file

## Line Prefixes

- ` ` (space): Context line (unchanged)
- `-`: Line removed from original file
- `+`: Line added to modified file
- `\`: "No newline at end of file" indicator

## Complete Example

```diff
diff --git a/pom.xml b/pom.xml
index 1234567..abcdefg 100644
--- a/pom.xml
+++ b/pom.xml
@@ -52,12 +52,8 @@
   </url>
  </organization>
  <properties>
-  <toolsjar>
-   ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar
-  </toolsjar>
+  <!-- tools.jar removed in JDK 9+ -->
  </properties>
  <dependencies>
-  <dependency>
-   <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
-   <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
-   <version>1.8</version>
-   <scope>system</scope>
-   <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
-  </dependency>
  </dependencies>
```

## Creating Patches

### Using git diff
```bash
# Diff between working directory and HEAD
git diff > my-changes.diff

# Diff between two commits
git diff commit1 commit2 > changes.diff

# Diff specific file
git diff path/to/file > file-changes.diff

# Diff staged changes
git diff --cached > staged.diff
```

### Using GNU diff
```bash
# Compare two files
diff -u original.txt modified.txt > changes.diff

# Compare directories recursively
diff -urN original/ modified/ > changes.diff
```

## Applying Patches

### Using git apply
```bash
# Apply patch
git apply patch.diff

# Check if patch applies cleanly (dry run)
git apply --check patch.diff

# Apply with 3-way merge
git apply -3 patch.diff
```

### Using patch command
```bash
# Apply patch
patch -p1 < patch.diff

# Reverse a patch
patch -R -p1 < patch.diff

# Dry run
patch --dry-run -p1 < patch.diff
```

## Strip Levels (-p flag)

The `-p` flag controls path stripping:

```diff
--- a/src/main/file.txt
+++ b/src/main/file.txt
```

- `-p0`: Keep full path `a/src/main/file.txt`
- `-p1`: Strip one level `src/main/file.txt` (most common)
- `-p2`: Strip two levels `main/file.txt`

## Best Practices

1. **Include context**: Default 3 lines of context helps patches apply cleanly
2. **Use unified format**: `-u` flag for diff, standard for Git
3. **Test patches**: Always use `--check` or `--dry-run` before applying
4. **Document changes**: Include descriptive commit messages
5. **One logical change per patch**: Makes review and application easier

## Common Issues

### Patch doesn't apply
- **Line endings**: Unix (LF) vs Windows (CRLF) differences
- **Whitespace**: Tabs vs spaces, trailing whitespace
- **Path differences**: Use correct `-p` level
- **File moved**: Patch refers to old location

**Solutions**:
```bash
# Ignore whitespace
git apply --whitespace=fix patch.diff

# Try different strip levels
patch -p0 < patch.diff
patch -p1 < patch.diff

# Force application (dangerous)
patch --force -p1 < patch.diff
```

## Creating Clean Diffs

For standardized, portable patches:

```bash
# Use unified format with context
diff -u -w original.txt modified.txt

# For directories
diff -urN -x '*.class' -x 'target' original/ modified/
```

**Flags**:
- `-u`: Unified format
- `-r`: Recursive
- `-N`: Treat absent files as empty
- `-w`: Ignore whitespace
- `-x`: Exclude pattern

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
    <artifactId>auto-parent</artifactId>
    <version>3</version>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.auto.value</groupId>
  <artifactId>auto-value</artifactId>
  <version>1.2-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>AutoValue</name>
  <description>
    Immutable value-type code generation for Java 1.6+.
  </description>

  <properties>
    <guava.version>18.0</guava.version>
  </properties>
  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto.service</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.ow2.asm</groupId>
      <artifactId>asm</artifactId>
      <version>4.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <!-- test dependencies -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.velocity</groupId>
      <artifactId>velocity</artifactId>
      <version>1.7</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava-testlib</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.6</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.11</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>src/main/java</directory>
      </resource>
    </resources>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
        <configuration>
          <addTestClassPath>true</addTestClassPath>
          <cloneProjectsTo>${project.build.directory}/it</cloneProjectsTo>
          <filterProperties>
            <auto.version>${project.version}</auto.version>
          </filterProperties>
          <pomIncludes>
            <pomInclude>*/pom.xml</pomInclude>
          </pomIncludes>
          <streamLogs>true</streamLogs>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>integration-test</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>install</goal>
              <goal>run</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.immutables.tools</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3</version>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <phase>package</phase>
            <goals>
              <goal>shade</goal>
            </goals>
            <configuration>
              <minimizeJar>true</minimizeJar>
              <relocations>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>org.objectweb</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.org.objectweb$</shadedPattern>
                </relocation>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>com.google</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.com.google$</shadedPattern>
                  <excludes>
                    <exclude>com.google.auto.value.**</exclude>
                  </excludes>
                </relocation>
              </relocations>
            </configuration>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS
======================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
Build System: Maven
Java Version: OpenJDK 11.0.27

ERROR SUMMARY
-------------
Build fails with the following error:
"Could not resolve dependencies for project com.google.auto:auto-common:jar:1.0-SNAPSHOT:
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

ROOT CAUSE
----------
The build failure is caused by incompatibility between JDK 11 and the Maven configuration.

1. The system is running JDK 11, which does NOT have tools.jar file
   - In JDK 8 and earlier: Compiler tools were in lib/tools.jar
   - In JDK 9+: tools.jar was removed; tools moved to java.compiler and jdk.compiler modules

2. The parent POM (pom.xml in /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml)
   defines two Maven profiles that set the ${toolsjar} property:
   - default-profile: Activates when ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar EXISTS
   - mac-profile: Activates when ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar EXISTS

3. Since neither file exists in JDK 11, NEITHER profile activates,
   leaving ${toolsjar} property UNDEFINED

4. The compile-testing library (used as test dependency in common, factory, service, value modules)
   has a system-scoped dependency on com.sun:tools:jar that references ${toolsjar}:

   <dependency>
     <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
     <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
     <version>${java.version}</version>
     <scope>system</scope>
     <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
   </dependency>

5. When Maven tries to resolve this dependency with an undefined ${toolsjar},
   it defaults to looking for tools.jar relative to the JDK installation, which fails

ERROR LOCATION
--------------
Configuration errors are in:
- /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml (parent POM)
  Lines 167-208: Profile definitions that don't handle JDK 9+

AFFECTED MODULES
----------------
All modules that depend on compile-testing (test scope):
- common/pom.xml (line 55-59: compile-testing 0.7)
- factory/pom.xml (line 72-76: compile-testing 0.8)
- service/pom.xml (line 55-59: compile-testing 0.6)
- value/pom.xml (line 80-84: compile-testing 0.6)

SOLUTION APPROACH
-----------------
The parent POM needs to be fixed to handle JDK 9+ where tools.jar doesn't exist.

Option 1 (Recommended): Add a JDK 9+ profile with a safe default for ${toolsjar}
- Add a new profile that activates for JDK [9,)
- Set ${toolsjar} to ${java.home} (which always exists) or similar safe value
- This prevents the undefined property error

Option 2: Remove the profiles entirely and set a safe default in <properties>
- Set <toolsjar>${java.home}</toolsjar> directly
- The compile-testing dependency will still fail to find the actual tools,
  but may handle it gracefully for test compilation

Option 3: Upgrade to newer compile-testing versions
- Newer versions may handle JDK 9+ better
- However, this requires version bumps which may cause other compatibility issues

Recommended fix: Option 1 - Add JDK 9+ profile

content.text:
I can see that `com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27:system` is being resolved. The path shows `/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar` which means it's still using the wrong path from the parent's default-profile.

The real issue is that in Maven, when both child and parent have properties with the same name, and both profiles are active, the LAST profile processed wins. Since parent profiles are processed after child profiles, the parent's value overwrites the child's.

The solution is to make our profile override by ensuring the parent's default-profile doesn't activate. We need to check the effective POM more carefully. Actually, let me try a different approach - we can exclude the tools dependency entirely from compile-testing since it's optional for test compilation on JDK 11+:

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS
======================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
Build System: Maven
Java Version: OpenJDK 11.0.27

ERROR SUMMARY
-------------
Build fails with the following error:
"Could not resolve dependencies for project com.google.auto:auto-common:jar:1.0-SNAPSHOT:
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

ROOT CAUSE
----------
The build failure is caused by incompatibility between JDK 11 and the Maven configuration.

1. The system is running JDK 11, which does NOT have tools.jar file
   - In JDK 8 and earlier: Compiler tools were in lib/tools.jar
   - In JDK 9+: tools.jar was removed; tools moved to java.compiler and jdk.compiler modules

2. The parent POM (pom.xml in /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml)
   defines two Maven profiles that set the ${toolsjar} property:
   - default-profile: Activates when ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar EXISTS
   - mac-profile: Activates when ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar EXISTS

3. Since neither file exists in JDK 11, NEITHER profile activates,
   leaving ${toolsjar} property UNDEFINED

4. The compile-testing library (used as test dependency in common, factory, service, value modules)
   has a system-scoped dependency on com.sun:tools:jar that references ${toolsjar}:

   <dependency>
     <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
     <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
     <version>${java.version}</version>
     <scope>system</scope>
     <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
   </dependency>

5. When Maven tries to resolve this dependency with an undefined ${toolsjar},
   it defaults to looking for tools.jar relative to the JDK installation, which fails

ERROR LOCATION
--------------
Configuration errors are in:
- /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml (parent POM)
  Lines 167-208: Profile definitions that don't handle JDK 9+

AFFECTED MODULES
----------------
All modules that depend on compile-testing (test scope):
- common/pom.xml (line 55-59: compile-testing 0.7)
- factory/pom.xml (line 72-76: compile-testing 0.8)
- service/pom.xml (line 55-59: compile-testing 0.6)
- value/pom.xml (line 80-84: compile-testing 0.6)

SOLUTION APPROACH
-----------------
The parent POM needs to be fixed to handle JDK 9+ where tools.jar doesn't exist.

Option 1 (Recommended): Add a JDK 9+ profile with a safe default for ${toolsjar}
- Add a new profile that activates for JDK [9,)
- Set ${toolsjar} to ${java.home} (which always exists) or similar safe value
- This prevents the undefined property error

Option 2: Remove the profiles entirely and set a safe default in <properties>
- Set <toolsjar>${java.home}</toolsjar> directly
- The compile-testing dependency will still fail to find the actual tools,
  but may handle it gracefully for test compilation

Option 3: Upgrade to newer compile-testing versions
